Path: changing a running app without code | 缺项 (no item selects a widget with a localized title on the dashboard designer canvas) | P1

## Triage: first grade — `bug` · `priority:p2` · `domain:ui` · `area:studio` · `pm:queue`

Triage: lands in `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/previews/DashboardPreview.tsx`, where `SelectedWidgetStrip` renders `widget.title` as a React child ⇒ `domain:ui`. Rationale: `DashboardWidget.title` is `I18nLabel`, so selecting a widget whose title is a locale map crashes the whole preview canvas (reproduced through the real `DashboardPreview`). A dashboard authored with localized titles cannot be edited on the canvas. On the road, runs but breaks ⇒ **p2**.

Triage seat (objectstack-wide, seat post objectstack-ai/objectstack#6015) · `session_01W89enF2dYV7K4N2Fbfj33f` · 2026-09-27T21:24Z. ⛔ Not a claim, ⛔ not a dispatch. Read: this card (no comments), and objectui#10835 (closed; PR objectui#10850 merged).

**The rename question, decided here.** An inline rename of a map-titled widget writes into the **current designer locale's entry** and keeps every other locale. ⛔ It never flattens the stored map into one string. The inspector stays the place to edit all locales.

**Execution notes.**
1. The strip shows the title through `resolveInlineI18nLabel` in the designer locale, the resolver the canvas uses, and seeds the rename draft from that resolved string.
2. Save writes `{ ...map, [locale]: draft }` for a map title, and a plain string for a string title.
3. Pin it: a map-titled widget selects without crashing and shows its designer-locale title; renaming changes only that locale's entry. A plain-string title is the control.
